To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bioglass nanowire (NW) reinforced poly (octanodiol citrate) elastomer (POC) composites were developed for bone tissue engineering application and showed improved cell growth and osteogenesis of mouse bone marrow mesengchymal stem cells.
bioglass nanosized particles can be incorporated into POC to form nanofiber composite and the composite exhibits improved mechanical properties, as well as enhanced osteoconductivity.

the POC/bioactive glass nanofiber composite supported the osteogenic differentiations of MSCs and the level of osteogenic differentiation was increased with increasing amount (5, 15 and 20%) of bioactive glass nanofibers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel bioglass nanocomposites based on POC elastomer and their potential for bone regeneration.
the fabrication of POC/bioactive glass nanofiber composit.
the fabrication and characterization of POC/bio-glass nanofiber nanocomposites and their osteoblast response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the POC/bioactive glass composites are excellent biomaterials for bone regeneration.
the POC/bioactive glass nanofiber composite is an excellent biomaterial with the potential to support the growth and differentiation of MSCs.
POC/bi-glass nanofiber nanocomposite scaffolds can be a promising biomaterial for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the POC/bio-glass nanofiber is a good biomaterial candidate for tissue regeneration.
the POC/5% bioglass nanocomposite would be the best candidate for the application of bone tissue engineering.
the incorporation of bioglass into POC matrix could increase the mechanical strength of POC, which could be used to fabricate a scaffold for bone tissue engineering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the POC/bioactive glass composite can be a promising candidate material for tissue engineering applications.

the addition of bioceramic particles to the POC matrix increased the glass transition temperatures and mechanical properties of the composite, while the addition of biocompatible bioglass nanoscale particles enhanced the osteogenic differentiation and bone mineralization of MSCs.
bioglass nanocomposites can be used as a biomaterial for bone tissue engineering.
